transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I just... well, I came in because my body feels completely drained. I mean, I'm sure I'm just a little worn out from work and I don't want to make a big deal out of nothing, but it's gotten to the point where even just walking from my car to the clinic today, or, um, just sitting down and trying to open the EHR at work... it just takes absolutely everything I have right now. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I made an appointment for that.
How long have you been feeling this level of fatigue?

Um, well, I feel bad saying it because I know I probably should have come in a lot sooner, I'm sorry. But, um... I guess this really exhausted, kind of down and guilty feeling has been going on for about nine months now? 

It started right after I had this, um, this stretch of time where I had just a ton of energy, and then I just completely crashed. I really hope it's okay that I waited so long to make an appointment. Am I explaining that right?
You mentioned a stretch of time where you had a ton of energy, did you feel unusually happy or elevated during that period?

Um, well... I guess you could say that. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm bragging or anything, but yeah, some days I just felt absolutely amazing. Like, unstoppable, you know? I was getting so much done at work and I just felt really good about myself. I hope that doesn't sound weird. 

But then... well, I feel terrible even admitting this, because I really try to be a good team player at the clinic... but if one of the nurses corrected my documentation, or, um, if someone just told me to slow down a little, I would just... I'd kind of snap at them. It felt like they were insulting me, even though I know they were just trying to help. I feel so bad about it now, I really do. I'm usually not like that at all. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a horrible person.
Have you been having any thoughts of worthlessness or feeling like you're a burden to others during this time?

Um... yeah. I feel terrible even saying it, because I really try my best not to be a bother to anyone, but... yes. I just feel so useless lately. 

I'm sure I'm probably just overthinking things, I know I shouldn't let it get to me, but... I keep replaying every single chart I do, and every set of vitals I take, just over and over in my head. I get this horrible feeling that I messed up and hurt the patients somehow. My supervisors are really great, and they keep telling me that nothing bad happened and I didn't do anything wrong, but... I just can't shake this awful guilt, like I'm doing damage and just dragging the whole team down. 

I hope I don't sound completely ridiculous saying that. I really want to be a good employee. Is it okay that I'm telling you this?
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that others can't, during this time?

Um... well, I really don't want to make it sound like I'm crazy or anything, because I promise I'm really trying my best to stay focused at work. I know how important it is to be fully present for the patients. But, um... I guess I have had a couple of weird things happen? 

I hope you don't think less of me for saying this, but sometimes during my shifts, I would... I would hear my name being called over the clinic speaker. Or, um, I'd hear a monitor beeping, like a patient was calling for me. And I'd go rushing over to check, because I really want to make sure everyone is okay, but... nobody else heard it. And the patient wasn't actually calling for me. 

I'm probably just working too hard or letting my stress get the better of me, right? I really hope it doesn't mean I'm doing a bad job. I just want to be helpful. Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that sounds really strange.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself during this time?

Um... no, no, not at all. I mean, I know I've been feeling really down and guilty about everything, but I would never... I would never do anything like that. I know how much that would hurt my family, and I'd never want to put them through that kind of pain. Plus, I know my team at the clinic needs me, even if I feel like I'm messing up sometimes. 

I really try to focus on being a good person and doing my best, you know? I hope you don't think I'm the kind of person who would... well, you know. I'm really trying hard to get better. Is it okay that I said no to that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your movement or activity level, such as feeling restless or having trouble sitting still?

Um... well, actually, it was kind of the opposite of being restless? I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, because I promise I always try to work as hard as I can, but... um... people at work actually told me I looked really slowed down. 

And I guess I could feel it, too. It's so embarrassing to admit, but even just... just putting a blood pressure cuff away, or trying to answer a simple question, it just took me way longer than normal to do it. I felt terrible about it because I know the nurses rely on me to be quick and efficient, and I really hope my coworkers didn't think I was just being lazy. I really was trying my best to keep up. 

Does that answer your question okay? I'm sorry if that wasn't what you were expecting me to say.
How often do you experience these feelings of worthlessness or guilt?

Um... well, it's pretty much all the time lately. I really don't want to sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself, because I know I have a good job and I should be grateful. But, um... it's just really hard to shake this feeling that I'm doing everything wrong. 

I just... I keep replaying every chart and every set of vitals in my head, over and over. I get so scared that I've hurt the patients somehow. I mean, my supervisors keep telling me that nothing bad happened and that I'm doing fine, and I really want to believe them because I respect them so much, but... I just can't stop feeling like I'm a burden to everyone there. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really silly since they already told me I didn't do anything wrong. I really am trying to be better about it and not let it affect my work. Is it normal to feel like that even when people tell you you're doing okay? I just hope I'm not letting everyone down.
Have you been feeling fidgety or having trouble sitting still lately?

Um... well, earlier I was saying how I felt slowed down, but... there was also a time before that when I guess I was kind of the opposite? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm contradicting myself, I just want to give you the whole picture so you can help me. 

But, um, a while back, I actually had so much energy I couldn't sit still at all. I was just... I kept walking the halls at the clinic, reorganizing all the supplies, checking the rooms over and over. I just kept looking for more things to do, even after my shift was supposed to be over. I just wanted to be really helpful to the nurses, you know? I wanted to make sure everything was perfect for them. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I was being disruptive or anything. I really was just trying to do a good job and be a team player. Is it okay that I was doing all that extra work? I just thought it was a good thing to have that much energy, but maybe I overdid it?
Can you tell me more about how often these episodes of feeling down and guilty happen, are they constant or do they come and go?

Um... well, it's pretty constant right now. I really hope I'm not complaining too much, because I know everyone gets sad sometimes, but... um... this depressed and guilty feeling, and just being so exhausted all the time... it's been going on for a really long time. 

I guess it started right after that really high-energy period I was just telling you about? Like, I just sort of... crashed after that. And it's been about nine months now that I've been feeling this way. I really try to put on a brave face at work and not let it show, because I don't want to bring anyone else down. I want to be a positive person to be around, you know? 

But it just hasn't really gone away for those nine months. Is it okay that it's lasted that long? I'm sorry if I should have been able to snap out of it by now, I really am trying my best to get back to normal.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing?

Um... I guess so? I mean, I don't want to sound ungrateful for the things I have, because I know I'm lucky to have hobbies and stuff, but... lately, I just haven't really felt like doing much of anything. 

I used to love playing video games with my friends online, or even just going for a run after work, but... I don't know, it just feels like too much effort now. I usually just end up sitting on my bed or sleeping. I really try to force myself to join them sometimes because I want to be a good friend and not flake out on them, but... I just don't get that same happy feeling from it anymore. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy. I really do want to enjoy those things again, I just... I don't know why I can't right now. Is that a normal part of feeling so down for this long? I'm sorry, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing?

Um... wait, I think we just talked about that, right? The... the video games and running? I'm so sorry, I hope I didn't confuse you or explain it badly the first time. I really try to be clear, but my brain is just... it's a little foggy these days. 

But yeah, I haven't really been doing any of my hobbies. I just don't have the energy for it. Did I... did I answer that okay before? I can try to explain it differently if you need me to, I really don't mind. I just want to be helpful.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Um... not really, no. I mean, I try to look forward to things, I really do. I don't want to be a downer for the people around me, so I'll agree to go to the movies or out to dinner when my friends ask. And I smile and tell them I'm excited, because I know they're just trying to be nice and include me. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... I don't actually feel that excitement inside. It's more just... going through the motions, I guess? I really hope that doesn't make me sound unappreciative of them. I'm trying my best to find the good in things, it's just... nothing really sparks that happy feeling right now. Is it okay that I don't have anything I'm really looking forward to? I feel bad even admitting that.
Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that others can't, in addition to hearing your name being called or monitors beeping?

Um... well, no, I don't think I've seen anything like that. I really hope I'm not making things sound worse than they are, but... the hearing things is mostly what happens. 

Like I was saying, it's usually just at work. I'm a support worker at a clinic, and... well, I'd be on my shift, and I swear I'd hear my name being called over the clinic speaker. Or, um, I'd hear a patient's monitor beeping, like it was signaling for me specifically. So I'd go rushing over to check on them, or look for whoever was calling me, but... nobody else heard it. And the patients weren't actually calling for me. 

I really try to do a good job at work, I swear I do. I just... I guess my brain was just playing tricks on me because I wanted to be helpful and attentive? I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or like I'm bad at my job. I really do care about the patients. Is it... is it normal to get a little confused like that when you're stressed?
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt relatively okay, without the overwhelming feelings of guilt and worthlessness?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I try to have good days, I really do. I don't want to complain, because I know I have a good job and I should be grateful. But... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I'm doing everything wrong. 

Like... I keep replaying every chart I've done, every set of vitals I've taken, just over and over in my head. And I get this awful feeling that I missed something, or that I hurt one of the patients. My supervisors are so nice, they keep telling me nothing bad happened and that I'm doing fine, but... I just feel so guilty all the time, like I'm a burden to everyone at the clinic. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds so silly, worrying about things when I'm being told it's okay. I really am trying to be better about it. Do you think... is it okay that I worry this much? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job.
Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions or thoughts that aren't based in reality?

Um... well... I'm a little embarrassed to even bring this up, because I really don't want you to think I'm arrogant or disrespectful to my bosses. I promise I'm usually really good at following directions and knowing my place. But... um... 

There was a time recently where I got... well, I got completely convinced that I had been chosen to fix how the whole clinic takes care of patients. Like, I thought it was my special, personal mission to completely overhaul the system. And... I know how silly this sounds now, because I'm just an 18-year-old right out of high school, but it felt so incredibly real to me. 

My supervisor actually had to pull me aside and tell me to stop, and she reminded me that I'm just an aide in training. Which is completely true, and she was really nice about it! But... at the time, I couldn't see that. I actually felt like she was just trying to block my mission, like they were all getting in the way of what I was meant to do. 

I feel so awful about it now, looking back. I really hope they don't think I'm a bad employee or that I think I'm better than the doctors and nurses. I just got so swept up in wanting to help everyone. Is it... I mean, does that make me sound completely out of my mind? I really was just trying to do a good thing for the clinic, I swear.
How often do you have days where you feel like you're at your lowest point, with the strongest feelings of guilt and worthlessness?

Um... well, it's pretty much been every day lately. I really wish I could say it wasn't, because I know I should be more positive. But... after all that energy I had just sort of... dropped, I started feeling really empty most days. Just sort of hopeless. 

I try to keep a smile on my face at work, I really do, but inside I just keep thinking that I've already ruined my future in healthcare before it even really started. I mean, I'm only 18, and I feel like I've already messed everything up. I hope you don't think I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I know other people have it so much worse, and I really should just push through it. Is it normal to feel this... this empty after having so much energy? I'm really trying my best to snap out of it.
Have you had any periods of at least two weeks where you felt relatively okay, without these overwhelming feelings of guilt and worthlessness, in the past year?

Um... well, to be honest... no. I really haven't had a break from it. I wish I could say I did, because I know I should be bouncing back better than this. 

Ever since I crashed after that... that time where I had all that energy and thought I was supposed to fix the clinic... the depressed, guilty, exhausted part has just stayed with me. It's been about nine months now. 

I really try not to let it show, and I hope I'm not coming across as someone who just wallows in it, because I really do try to push past it every single day. I just... I haven't had a good stretch of weeks where I felt normal again since then. Does that... I mean, is it okay that it's lasted that long? I'm sorry I haven't been able to shake it off faster.
Have you experienced any other hallucinations or delusions besides hearing your name being called or monitors beeping?

Um... no, no, nothing else besides that. And... um, I really want to make sure I explain this right, because I don't want you to think I'm completely out of touch with reality all the time. I know how bad it sounds. But all of that stuff... the hearing my name, the monitors beeping, and that whole embarrassing idea about my special medical mission... it really only happened when I was completely wired. 

Like, during that time when I was barely sleeping at all and running around trying to overhaul the clinic. Once that huge burst of energy finally ended and I crashed... all of those weird thoughts and sounds completely stopped. I haven't heard anything like that or felt chosen like that since then. 

I mean... that's a good sign, right? That it went away when my energy dropped? I really hope that makes sense. I just... I don't want you to worry that I'm hearing things right now while I'm trying to do my job. I promise I'm completely grounded right now.
Are you currently experiencing any hallucinations or delusions?

Um... no, definitely not right now. I promise. 

I know I brought it up a second ago, but just to be completely honest with you about how it was... back then, during my shifts, I would hear my name over the clinic speaker, or... or I'd hear a monitor beeping for me when nobody else heard it. I'd actually go looking for a patient who wasn't even calling. 

I feel so stupid even admitting that out loud to you, I really do. I know how terrible that sounds for someone working in healthcare. But I swear it completely stopped when my energy crashed. I'm not experiencing anything like that right now, I promise. I really want to be reliable and do a good job at work, so I wouldn't hide it from you if it was still happening. I hope you believe me... I'm doing okay answering these questions, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
